_comment: Environment binding for the legacy-migrate OS. Copy to workspace.json and fill in real values.
workspace.json is gitignored: it holds absolute paths and internal hostnames, which must
never enter a tracked file of this public repository.
Skills read this file; they contain no environment constants of their own.

legacy.root: <abs path to the legacy PHP checkout>
legacy.treeRoot: <abs path to the source tree root that the paths in `ours` are relative to>
legacy.sourceRoot: <abs path to the migrated service's source root>
_ours: Directories this team owns, relative to treeRoot, each mapped to a short name.
Two hooks read it: the encoding guard warns before an edit outside these, and the
tooling hook groups its usage log by the name. Everything else in the tree belongs
to another team - read it freely, never edit it. Keeping it here rather than in the
hooks is what lets the hooks be tracked: a path from the legacy tree is company
information just as much as the code inside it.
_tooling: What the legacy-reading tools in .claude/scripts/ need in order to scope a search,
pick a PHP runtime, and build a definition index. These lived as constants inside
the scripts, which is the reason the scripts had to sit in the gitignored checkout;
moving them here is what lets the scripts be tracked. Same trade the two hooks made.
treeMarker     - path, relative to `root`, that identifies the source tree. A tool
walks up from its own location looking for it, so it can be called
from anywhere. Also how `treeRoot` is checked for a typo.
services       - every tree a search can be scoped to, relative to treeRoot, each
mapped to a short name. Wider than `ours`: it includes trees another
team owns, which are read freely and never edited.
sharedLibrary  - which of those every service loads. Searched alongside whichever
service the caller is standing in, because a service reaches exactly
two trees: itself and this one.
primaryService - the service being migrated. The answer when the caller stands outside
any service, and the default target when an index is built.
runtimes       - PHP version per service prefix, and the container image that version
is checked in. The local php binary proves nothing about a runtime it
does not match, so the linter shells out to these instead. A prefix
with no entry is reported as not checked, never as passing.
vendorGlobs    - trees inside the checkout holding third-party code, relative to
treeRoot. Never the answer to a search, so they are folded out.
Generic names (vendor, node_modules, bower_components) stay in the
script: those carry no company information.
legacy.treeMarker: <path under root that identifies the source tree>

<service-dir>.image: <image ref, pinned by digest where the tag can move>

<shared-library-dir>._comment: A tree loaded by two runtimes is checked on the lower one: code that parses there parses on the higher, and not the reverse.

vendorGlobs: <relative glob of a vendored tree that generic names do not cover>
_v2: The five sections below are what the v2 tools read. None of them is in _phpenc's
required-key list on purpose: the six legacy-reading tools must keep working in a
checkout that has not filled these in. Each new tool requires its own keys instead,
and stops with the key name when one is missing.
tooling.phpBinary  - php used for tokenising. `phpmove` runs it with
short_open_tag=1 and refuses to answer if that did not take:
a tree where 496 files open with `<?` is read as plain HTML
otherwise, and comes back with zero violations.
swap.*             - what the allowed page shape is, expressed as patterns rather
than as names, so this file stays free of company identifiers.
snapshot.*         - how a captured page is normalized before comparison, and what
dualRun.*          - where the PHP experiment helper appends its JSONL, what env
var carries that path into the container, and which page can
be read back to learn the toggle's current mode.
switch.values.dual - the third mode. It must equal MigrationExperiment.php's
_pagecheck: The three keys below have exactly one consumer each: `pagecheck`. They are the
two instrumentation variables and the coverage artifact, and each of them exists
because the stage that needs it must be able to FAIL rather than be skipped.
dualRun.noiseEnvVar   - stage 2. Set non-empty, the helper runs the legacy body
against itself and logs the diff keys that move between
two runs of the same code. That is the run-to-run difference,
and without it an equivalence loop cannot tell its own jitter
from a missing rule. Must equal the helper's NOISE_ENV.
dualRun.fakeValueEnvVar  - stage 5. Set non-empty in `migrated`, the helper runs the
legacy body but throws its return value away. The capture
taken then must be byte-identical to the migrated
baseline; anything that moves is a screen value that still
comes from PHP. Must equal the helper's FAKEVALUE_ENV.
dualRun.coveragePath  - stage 6. Host path of the JSON that Xdebug coverage is
collected into, shaped like xdebug_get_code_coverage():
{"<abs file>": {"<line>": <hits>}}. When Xdebug is absent
the stage is SKIPPED and says so in state.json; when Xdebug
is present but this file never appears, the stage exits 3.
Neither of those is a pass.
Leave all three empty in a checkout that has not wired them: the stage that needs
one stops with the key name rather than reporting a narrow answer.

swap.functionsDir: <relative dir under a surface docroot where swap service files live>
swap.callPattern: <regex matching the swap service call, e.g. a class::method form>
swap.templateRenderPattern: <optional regex: template *object* calls (construct/set/fetch). Omit only if this tree renders templates by include alone - without it those statements are reported as violations>
swap.viewVarPattern: <optional regex matching the names of view-wiring variables an included header or template reads. Those assignments carry no rule for the swap to take, so extraction never removes them; without this key "zero violations" is unreachable on a tree that has them. Match by NAME, never by statement shape - a literal assignment to a view variable and one to a domain parameter are the same tokens>
guardIdioms: <regex: redirect-script idiom that ends in an early exit>

snapshot.errorMarker: <regex that appears on an error page>

dualRun.logPath: <abs path of the JSONL the PHP helper appends to (must be mounted into the container)>
dualRun.readbackPath: /<relative path of a page that prints the current toggle mode - one token, nothing else>
dualRun.coveragePath: <abs path of the JSON Xdebug coverage is collected into, or "" if not wired>

legacy._surfaces: one entry per SURFACE: one legacy site, with its own docroot, host, charset, session and logged-out marker. `--surface` names one of these keys, and `scope: surface` in a round record means an entry true only on this one.

<surface-a>.loggedOutMarker: <regex matching the body of an unauthenticated response - this surface answers 200, so a status code proves nothing>
<surface-a>.charset: <charset to decode a diff with; the first of this, utf-8 and cp949 that succeeds wins>

docker.composeDir: <abs path to the dir holding docker-compose.yml>
docker.envFile: <abs path to the compose .env file that carries migration toggles>

_javaHome: JDK the Gradle build must run under. Required, not optional: a newer JDK than the
wrapper supports fails with a one-line error that names only the version number,
which reads like anything but a toolchain problem. Everything that shells out to
backend.javaHome: <abs path to the JDK home the build requires>
_modules: proxy is the BFF: it exposes the client-facing surface and holds no domain logic.
fixity is the domain service: models, invariants, policies, use cases, persistence.
_architecture: How the repo enforces its layer layout as an executable rule, not a document.
architectureRules is what the designer and implementer read to learn the constraint;
point it at the module or test that states the rules, whose own tests say what each
rule means. architectureCheck is how anyone runs it standalone. The build must also
run it, or the constraint is advice rather than a gate.
backend.architectureRules: <relative path to the module or test holding the layer rules>

basicAuth._comment: Which account each surface authenticates as. Credentials are read at runtime from the backend config, never stored here.

_startup: What the domain service needs before it can boot. It fetches its DB settings from a
remote config service over TLS, so a missing truststore looks like a build failure
rather than a missing prerequisite. The password here is the JKS default, not a
secret; real credentials come from the config service at runtime.

fixityUrl._comment: How the BFF is told where the domain service is. Reassigning the domain service port means moving this too, or the BFF boots healthy and returns nothing.

_storageState: Playwright storageState JSON per surface. `htmlsnap` reads the cookies out of it
rather than logging in: issuing a session is a solved problem in that repo, and a
capture tool that logs in is a capture tool that can silently capture a login page.

storageState.<surface-a>: <abs path to that surface's storageState json>

<surface-a>.baseUrlEnv: <env var that overrides the surface base URL>

docs.root: <abs path where page artifacts and domain docs are written>
docs._pagesDir: directory under docs.root holding one directory per page. The VALUE names a directory in your repository, not a word this OS chose - do not rewrite it to match the key
docs._designDir: where the area-level design lives. Consumer: legacy-migrate Phase 3 (D-25)
docs._recordDir: where the per-role round records live. Consumers: ctxevolve, each agent (D-28)

_comment: Optional. If a richer OS already exists elsewhere, name the skills to delegate to
instead of reimplementing (D-09). Empty means this repo runs standalone.
Each key has exactly one consumer, so an unread key is a bug, not a spare:
skillsDir    - the directory the three below are resolved in
startBackend - local-stack, for bringing the backend up
runE2e       - legacy-migrate, for the Phase 2 baseline and the Phase 6 loop
writeE2e     - observation-author, for authoring the spec
